newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican feeder head weekly exports, imports - USDA.
newsitem.headline: Mexican feeder head weekly exports, imports - USDA.

text.p: USDA said Friday that steer calves exported to the United States from Mexico sold two to three cents/lb higher than last week and yearlings were sold steady to one cent/lb higher.
Exports for the week were estimated at 10,000 head into Texas and New Mexico states. Confirmed exports for the previous week totaled 6,018 head, against 4,786 head in the same week in 1996.
"Trade active, demand very good. Thirty percent of cattle crossed were previously sold on video," USDA said.
Prices for feeder steers weighing 300-400 lb were 92-102 cents/lb, for 400-500 lb they were 82-92 cents/lb.
The USDA estimated 2,500 head of slaughter cows were imported from Mexico for the week.
